sentences.en: I want to start in medias res.
sentences.zh: 我想直接切入正题。

sentences.en: So I want to start in Munich on the 18th of February, 1943, at the university, at the great university in Munich.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算从1943年2月18日的慕尼黑讲起，在大学里，慕尼黑那所宏伟的大学里。

sentences.en: And I want to start with a man called Jakob Schmidt, who was the caretaker of the building, a kind of ordinary Bavarian bloke.
sentences.zh: 我想从一个叫雅各布·施密特的人讲起，他是那栋建筑的看门人，一个普通的巴伐利亚老百姓。

sentences.en: He is middle-aged.
sentences.zh: 他正值中年。

sentences.en: He is a loyal Nazi party member, a very keen party member, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他是纳粹党的忠实党员，非常狂热的党员。

sentences.en: And he's the caretaker.
sentences.zh: 而他正是那里的看门人。

sentences.en: It's a lovely kind of warm, sort of early spring day, sort of unseasonably warm.
sentences.zh: 那是一个可爱、温暖的初春日子，天气出奇的暖和。

sentences.en: So all is right with the world, as he sees it.
sentences.zh: 所以在他的眼里，一切都那么美好。

sentences.en: And the war's not going very well, of course, because the Germans have had very bad news from Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 当然，战争并不太顺利，因为德国人从斯大林格勒收到了非常糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: But he's just sort of minding his own business as the caretaker of the building.
sentences.zh: 但他作为建筑的看门人，只是在管好自己的事情。

sentences.en: The students have all arrived.
sentences.zh: 学生们都已经到了。

sentences.en: They've gone into their lectures and their classes.
sentences.zh: 他们去上讲座和课程了。

sentences.en: And at about 11 o'clock, two people come into the great sort of hall, the great inner courtyard, which has this great glass vaulted ceiling.
sentences.zh: 大约11点左右，两个人走进了那个巨大的大厅，也就是拥有巨大拱形玻璃天花板的巨大内部庭院。

sentences.en: And he kind of vaguely notices them, but doesn't think anything of it.
sentences.zh: 他隐约注意到了他们，但没多想。

sentences.en: And a few moments later, he sees a whole load of paper
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，他看到一大堆纸

sentences.en: floating down from the glass vaulted ceiling.
sentences.zh: 从拱形玻璃天花板上飘落下来。

sentences.en: And he looks up, Jakob Schmidt, and he sees that these two people, who he barely looked at, a young man and a young woman, are throwing pieces of paper, throwing leaflets down
sentences.zh: 雅各布·施密特抬头一看，发现这两个他几乎没怎么注意的年轻人——一个年轻男子和一个年轻女子，正在

sentences.en: from the gallery of this university sort of lobby.
sentences.zh: 从这所大学大堂的走廊上往下扔纸片、扔传单。

sentences.en: And he stares up at them and he shouts,
sentences.zh: 他瞪着他们大喊

sentences.en: stop, you know, you're under arrest, or words to that effect, because he's so shocked at them throwing this stuff around.
sentences.zh: 住手，你知道的，你们被捕了，或者类似的话，因为看到他们把这些东西到处乱扔，他感到太震惊了。

sentences.en: And at that very moment, the lecture halls, it's the end of the lectures.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，讲座大厅的课结束了。

sentences.en: So the doors fly open and suddenly there are people everywhere, you know, students coming out of the lectures.
sentences.zh: 所以大门猛地打开，突然到处都是人，你知道的，学生们从讲座里涌了出来。

sentences.en: And the two people that he's shouting at start to come down the stairs to kind of lose themselves amid the crowd.
sentences.zh: 他正冲着那两个人大喊，而那两人开始下楼，想在人群中隐匿踪迹。

sentences.en: But Jakob Schmidt is a man of great assiduousness.
sentences.zh: 但雅各布·施密特是一个非常一丝不苟的人。

sentences.en: So he keeps his eyes on them.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直盯着他们。

sentences.en: He pushes his way through the crowds and he manages to catch up with them and force his way toward them and grab them.
sentences.zh: 他在人群中挤来挤去，设法追上他们，强行朝他们靠过去并抓住了他们。

sentences.en: And he shouts again, stop, you're under arreSt.
sentences.zh: 他又大喊，住手，你们被捕了。

sentences.en: And everybody around is appalled, wondering what's going on.
sentences.zh: 周围所有人都惊呆了，不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And they don't try and run away.
sentences.zh: 而他们并没有试图逃跑。

sentences.en: They just stand there.
sentences.zh: 他们只是站在那里。

sentences.en: You know, they're frozen.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们僵住了。

sentences.en: Suddenly all the fight has gone out of them.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们所有的反抗意志都烟消云散了。

sentences.en: And he takes the two of them and he sort of drags them away to the university rector's office.
sentences.zh: 他把这两人带走，把他们拖到了大学校长的办公室。

sentences.en: And it's there that the authorities find out who they are.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，当局查明了他们的身份。

sentences.en: And they are a brother and sister called Hans and Sophie Scholl.
sentences.zh: 他们是一对兄妹，名叫汉斯和苏菲·朔尔。

sentences.zh: 它讲述的是汉斯和苏菲·朔尔的故事，以及他们所属的“白玫瑰”抵抗运动，还有他们是如何在1943年的那一天来到

sentences.en: at the Munich University building that day in 1943, throwing their leaflets around and about what happened to them afterwards.

sentences.zh: 我想苏菲当时22岁。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.

sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.zh: 他们是学生。

sentences.zh: 但这真是一个伟大的故事，对于理解虔诚基督徒与纳粹政权的关系具有非常有趣的意义。

sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.zh: 那他们是谁？

sentences.zh: 所以汉斯出生于1918年，

sentences.en: So as you say, they're in their early 20s.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们刚出头二十岁。

sentences.zh: 他们是罗伯特和玛格达莱娜·朔尔的孩子。

sentences.zh: 他们的父亲罗伯特·朔尔曾是德国西南部士瓦本地区一些小镇的镇长。

sentences.en: He is a sort of big, he's a big and very German looking man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个身材高大、很有德国人长相的男子。

sentences.zh: 他是一名税务顾问。

sentences.en: So not exactly the most sort of, no offense to our tax consultant fans or listeners, but perhaps not the most glamorous.
sentences.zh: 所以这算不上是最……无意冒犯我们当税务顾问的粉丝或听众，但这或许算不上最光鲜亮丽的职业。

sentences.en: We don't normally talk about tax consultants except for the Emperor Anastasius.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不会谈论税务顾问，除了阿纳斯塔修斯皇帝。

sentences.en: Very much friend of the show.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: Or I suppose Antonio Salazar.
sentences.zh: 或者我想还有安东尼奥·萨拉查。

sentences.en: But Robert Scholl, their father, so their mother Magdalena was a Protestant nurse and her Protestantism is very important to her.
sentences.zh: 但是他们的父亲罗伯特·朔尔，他们的母亲玛格达莱娜是一名新教护士，她的新教信仰对她非常重要。

sentences.en: Their father, he's also a man of a very sort of strong inner conviction.
sentences.zh: 他们的父亲，也是一个有着非常坚定的内心信念的人。

sentences.en: So in the First World War,
sentences.zh: 所以在第一次世界大战期间，

sentences.zh: 罗伯特·朔尔其实是一个和平主义者，他曾担任过医务兵。

sentences.en: So he hadn't seen action.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有亲历前线战火。

sentences.en: He'd done his bit for his country, but he didn't believe in violence.
sentences.zh: 他尽到了对国家的责任，但他不相信暴力。

sentences.en: There's a word in German for somebody with, like Robert Scholl, they call him an Eitzelgänger, a man who goes his own way, the man who goes on his own.
sentences.zh: 德语里有一个词用来形容像罗伯特·朔尔这样的人，他们称之为“独行者”，一个走自己路的人，一个孤军奋战的人。

sentences.en: So Nazi's not keen on that?
sentences.zh: 所以纳粹不太喜欢这种人？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.zh: However,

sentences.en: they're respectively,
sentences.zh: 分别

sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代初纳粹在德国掌权时，汉斯14岁，苏菲12岁。

sentences.en: And they both join with their sisters.
sentences.zh: 他们和姐妹们一起加入了。

sentences.en: They've got three, they've got two sisters and a brother.
sentences.zh: 他们有三个，他们有两个姐妹和一个兄弟。

sentences.en: The sisters,
sentences.zh: 姐妹们，

sentences.en: Inga and Elizabeth, and their brother is Werner.
sentences.zh: 英格和伊丽莎白，他们的兄弟是维尔纳。

sentences.en: And they join the Hitler Youth like so many, you know, children and teenagers do in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 像20世纪30年代的许多儿童和青少年一样，他们加入了希特勒青年团。

sentences.en: They love it, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, they do because they think like so many, again, like so many, they think it's a great lark, very exciting.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实很喜欢，因为和许多人一样，又一次，和许多人一样，他们觉得这像是一场恶作剧，非常刺激。

sentences.en: You get to dress up.
sentences.zh: 你还可以穿上制服。

sentences.en: So the Hitler Youth, to give you a sense of its great explosion, the end of 1932, it had about 100,000 members.
sentences.zh: 为了让你感受到希特勒青年团的发展规模之迅猛，到1932年底，它大约有10万名成员。

sentences.en: By 1935, it had 4 million.
sentences.zh: 到了1935年，成员达到了400万。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is obviously sort of coercion and getting in with the regime and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这其中显然有很多是出于强迫，是为了迎合政权以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But as you absolutely say, they're given a chance to dress up in uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说的那样，他们确实得到了穿上制服的机会。

sentences.en: They're given, they're going to go on torch-lit processions.
sentences.zh: 他们被安排去参加火炬游行。

sentences.en: And they genuinely believe in that they're rebuilding Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且他们真心相信自己是在重建德国。

sentences.en: So their sister,
sentences.zh: 所以他们的姐妹，

sentences.en: Well, they're only 12, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们才12岁，对吧？

sentences.zh: 他们的姐妹，

sentences.en: This impressed us and we listened with rapture.
sentences.zh: 这给我们留下了深刻印象，我们听得如痴如醉。

sentences.zh: 我们被告知，我们应该为比自身更伟大的事业而活。

sentences.zh: 而且以一种奇特的方式，我们受到了认真对待。

sentences.zh: 盛装打扮。

sentences.zh: 来参加野营吧。

sentences.en: It's going to be great fun.
sentences.zh: 那将会非常有趣。

sentences.en: And Hans,
sentences.zh: 还有汉斯，

sentences.en: he's really into this.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常热衷于此。

sentences.en: Sophie's into it too.
sentences.zh: 苏菲也很喜欢。

sentences.en: She loves all the hiking.
sentences.zh: 她特别喜欢徒步旅行。

sentences.en: She's very romantic,
sentences.zh: 她非常浪漫，

sentences.en: very idealistic.
sentences.zh: 非常具有理想主义。

sentences.en: She writes, there's this great tradition of kind of young people in Germany in the early 20th century getting out and enjoying nature and going on these sort of walks all together
sentences.zh: 她写道，在20世纪初的德国，年轻人走出家门、亲近自然、结伴远足有着非常悠久的传统

sentences.en: and this sort of collective

sentences.zh: 她非常喜欢这一切。

sentences.zh: 但他的孩子们根本不听。

sentences.zh: 所以汉斯加入后不久，就被任命为某种班长。

sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我的意思是，有些听众可能会觉得这是一个糟糕的类比，但我觉得并非完全不恰当。

sentences.en: And he is chosen because he's such a big, sort of a bigwig

sentences.en: And all the sort of, everyone says, of course, they've chosen Hans, he's so handsome, he's so, you know, he loves all this kind of thing.

sentences.en: And he said later to one of his sisters that he didn't like the fact that when he was at Nuremberg, there was no time and no opportunity to have proper conversations and debates
sentences.zh: 他后来对他的一个姐姐说，他不喜欢在纽伦堡时没有时间也没有机会进行适当的对话和辩论

sentences.en: about the future of Germany, that they were just sort of told what to do.
sentences.zh: 关于德国未来的讨论，他们只是被告知该做什么。

sentences.en: And they were being, you know, that it was all mindless.
sentences.zh: 而且他们当时正在……你知道的，这一切都是盲目的。

sentences.en: You know, the Shoal children, are terribly idealistic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，肖尔家的孩子们极具理想主义。

sentences.en: They're great ones for kind of not only going on these massive nature walks, but also sitting around and talking about the meaning of life.

sentences.en: And with their parents.

sentences.en: With their parents.
sentences.zh: 和他们的父母一起。

sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，极权主义的特点之一，特别是

sentences.zh: 纳粹极权主义，绝对是这样一种观念：家庭不应该成为进行私人谈话的安全空间，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they have the problem of the fact that their father, who they revere in many ways, who is this very inspiring man who goes his own way, that their father

sentences.en: But there's a couple of other things as well.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他一些事情。

sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，在某个时候

sentences.zh: 汉斯被发现阅读伟大的犹太作家斯蒂芬·茨威格的书。

sentences.en: And he clearly liked
sentences.zh: 他显然很喜欢

sentences.zh: 我猜是斯蒂芬·茨威格的短篇小说，它们非常易读且精彩，结构完美。

sentences.en: And he was obviously told by somebody, this is no good, he's a Jewish writer.
sentences.zh: 很显然有人告诉他，这不好，他是个犹太作家。

sentences.en: And that gave him kind of pause.
sentences.zh: 这让他有所停顿和思考。

sentences.en: But apparently, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但显然，我的意思是，

sentences.en: He decides that he's going to, he carried the banner at the Nuremberg rally and when he gets back to Ulm, he decides that as a project for his squad, they're going to design
sentences.zh: 他决定，他在纽伦堡集会上举了旗帜，当他回到乌尔姆后，他决定作为他们小队的一个项目，他们要设计

sentences.zh: 他们自己特殊的旗帜，这会让他们脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And he designs this very colourful banner of a griffin.
sentences.zh: 他设计了这面色彩斑斓的格里芬神兽旗。

sentences.zh: 基本上，他们带着格里芬旗走上乌尔姆街头，其他一些希特勒青年团的大人物看到他们后大惊失色，并把旗帜撕毁了。

sentences.en: And they tear it down not because they're offended by griffins, but because it's displaying individual, individuality of thought.
sentences.zh: 他们撕毁旗帜不是因为被格里芬冒犯了，而是因为它展示了独立思考的能力。

sentences.en: No, they've got nothing against griffins because it's individualism.
sentences.zh: 不，他们对格里芬本身没有意见，是因为这是个人主义。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's broken with the, you know, it's not what you're meant to have.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为这打破了……你知道的，这不是你该有的样子。

sentences.en: And Hans is really shocked by this and he has a fight with this bloke in the street.
sentences.zh: 汉斯对此感到非常震惊，并在街上和这家伙打了一架。

sentences.en: And from that point onwards, it's as though something within him is kind of broken and his faith in the party and in the mission and the enterprise.

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.zh: 苏菲遇到了一个问题。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种双马尾之类的好让自己看起来像个优秀的

sentences.en: German girl.
sentences.zh: 德国女孩。

sentences.zh: 而苏菲，她不是金发。

sentences.zh: 她不想留那种村姑的发型。

sentences.zh: 她留着波波头。

sentences.zh: 她留着短短的波波头。

sentences.zh: 这再次让她在人群中显得与众不同，你知道这对于青少年来说有多重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 关于你是要随大流，还是走自己的路、做一个不同的人的问题。

sentences.zh: 他们的父亲总是鼓励他们与众不同。

sentences.zh: 罗伯特·肖尔对他的孩子说，我希望你们在生活中正直而自由地行走，即使在前路艰难时也是如此。

sentences.en: We talked, didn't we, in our episode on teenagers a long time ago about how there was this trend under the Nazis for some teenagers
sentences.zh: 我们在很久以前关于青少年的那一期节目中讨论过，在纳粹统治下，有些青少年有一种趋势

sentences.zh: 我想，他们可以说是原生态的青少年。

sentences.zh: 他们正在探索与众不同的兴奋感。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The idea that to be different was what being a teenager is all about.

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，看看那些拖着旗帜慢吞吞行进的行尸走肉。

sentences.zh: 完全就是这样。

sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·茨威格式的时刻。

sentences.zh: 我们应该谈谈文学吗？

sentences.zh: 我们应该谈谈你们最喜欢的一些作家吗？

sentences.zh: 她说，哦，太棒了。

sentences.zh: 我要带一些海因里希·海涅的诗来，他是我最喜欢的作家之一。

sentences.zh: 接着是一片死寂、惊恐的沉默，因为海涅是犹太人。

sentences.zh: 而她，

sentences.en: you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: So again, you know, this marks her out as unusual.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，这使她显得与众不同。

sentences.zh: 因此，当我们接近20世纪30年代末时，他们已经对希特勒青年团彻底失望了。

sentences.zh: 这是一个名为DJ111的群体。

sentences.zh: 这代表着“1929年11月1日德国青年团”，

sentences.zh: 那一天，该团体的创始人曾在国外，然后回到了德国。

sentences.zh: 他决定成立一个青年组织，实际上是为了对抗他所看到的纳粹和希特勒青年团的崛起。

sentences.en: And so this group that Hans joins in Ulm to give you a sense of the kind of things they do.
sentences.zh: 所以汉斯在乌尔姆加入的这个组织，为了让你们了解他们所做的事情。

sentences.en: They love hitchhiking.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢搭便车旅行。

sentences.en: They love
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢

sentences.zh: 巴尔干民歌。

sentences.zh: 他们弹奏俄罗斯巴拉莱卡琴。

sentences.zh: 他们刻意保持着国际化。

sentences.zh: 他们全部使用小写字母来书写。

sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一件小事，但包豪斯就是这么做的。

sentences.zh: 他们做的另一件事是，这些

sentences.zh: 总之，

sentences.zh: 他作为医务兵被派往法国。

sentences.zh: 他后来在东线服役。

sentences.zh: 什么震惊了她？

sentences.zh: 所以索菲在某个时候说，嗯，她写信给远在
